description: ClickHouse cluster admin dashboard — on-call incident response. Default time range: 6h.
title: ClickHouse Admin

panels.title: Active Errors — system.errors
panels.description: Current errors with their last message across all nodes. Reset on server restart. Note: SQL panels use clusterAllReplicas('default', ...) — set the 'CH Cluster Name' variable to match your ClickHouse internal cluster name in remote_servers config.

targets.rawSql: SELECT name AS error, last_error_message AS message, value AS count, toDateTime(last_error_time) AS last_seen FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.errors) WHERE value > 0 ORDER BY last_error_time DESC LIMIT 30

panels.title: CPU Usage — per Pod
panels.description: CPU utilisation as a fraction of all available vCPUs (0–100%). OSUserTime + OSSystemTime report CPU-seconds/wall-second; dividing by OSNumVirtualCPUs normalises to a proper percentage.

panels.title: Storage Used (Hot) — per Pod
panels.description: Hot storage used per replica. Replicas on the same shard should be nearly equal — divergence indicates one replica has more/fewer merged parts, or TTL moves ran on only some nodes. If the gap grows over time, check merge lag and replication queue depth.

panels.title: Failed Queries/sec — per Pod
panels.description: Rate of failed queries per pod. A spike on one pod points to a bad replica.

panels.title: Insert Throughput — per Table
panels.description: Rows/sec per table from system.query_log.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfInterval(event_time, INTERVAL $__interval_s second) AS time, tables[1] AS table, sum(written_rows) / $__interval_s AS rows_per_sec FROM system.query_log WHERE event_time >= toDateTime(intDiv($__from, 1000)) AND event_time <= toDateTime(intDiv($__to, 1000)) AND type = 'QueryFinish' AND query_kind = 'Insert' AND length(tables) > 0 AND database != 'system' GROUP BY time, table ORDER BY time ASC

panels.title: Active Parts — per Table (Current Snapshot)
panels.description: Current part count per table. High part counts indicate merge lag.

targets.rawSql: SELECT database, table, count() AS active_parts, sum(rows) AS total_rows, formatReadableSize(sum(bytes_on_disk)) AS size_on_disk, max(modification_time) AS last_modified FROM system.parts WHERE active = 1 AND database != 'system' GROUP BY database, table ORDER BY active_parts DESC LIMIT 30

panels.title: Async Insert — Pending Queue Depth
panels.description: Pending async inserts buffered server-side. A growing queue risks data loss if the server restarts.

panels.title: Async Insert — Batch Size (Rows per Flush)
panels.description: Average number of rows batched per async insert flush. A low value (< 100) means clients are sending tiny inserts and async batching is not effective — consider tuning async_insert_max_data_size or async_insert_busy_timeout_ms.

panels.title: Query Latency (avg) — per Pod
panels.description: Average query duration in ms. ClickHouse does not expose latency histograms via Prometheus; p99 requires system.query_log.

panels.title: Merge Pool Saturation
panels.description: Active merges vs pool size (left axis). Saturation % on right axis. When saturation reaches 100% and part count is rising, merges cannot keep pace with inserts.

panels.title: Async Insert Buffered Flushes/sec
panels.description: Rate of async insert buffer flushes to disk. High flush rate means many small insert batches.

panels.title: Replication Queue Depth — per Replica
panels.description: Queue depth per replica (pod). Each row is one replica. Uses clusterAllReplicas to query all nodes simultaneously.

targets.rawSql: SELECT hostname() AS replica, database, table, count() AS queue_depth FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.replication_queue) GROUP BY replica, database, table ORDER BY queue_depth DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Replication Lag — per Replica
panels.description: Age of the oldest pending replication task per replica. Growing lag means a replica is falling behind.

targets.rawSql: SELECT hostname() AS replica, max(dateDiff('second', create_time, now())) AS lag_seconds FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.replication_queue) GROUP BY replica ORDER BY lag_seconds DESC

panels.title: ClickHouse Keeper — Liveness per Pod
panels.description: Shows ALIVE (green) if the pod has at least one active Keeper session, DEAD (red) if zero. Loss of Keeper connectivity stops all replication and DDL.

panels.title: S3 Storage Used
panels.description: Total bytes in S3 tiered storage. Adjust 's3' in metric name to match your S3 disk name.

panels.title: S3 GET Operations/sec
panels.description: S3 GET request rate per pod. Use the 'S3 GET Attribution' table below to break down by source (user queries, merges, TTL).

panels.title: S3 Merge Reads (bytes/sec)
panels.description: Bytes read from S3 by background merges on tiered data.

panels.title: S3 GET Attribution — by Source (selected time range)
panels.description: Breaks down S3 GET requests by what triggered them: user SELECT queries, merges/OPTIMIZE, TTL moves, or other internals. Helps diagnose unexpected S3 request spikes. Sourced from system.query_log ProfileEvents.

targets.rawSql: SELECT multiIf(query_kind = 'Select', 'User SELECT', query_kind = 'Insert', 'INSERT', match(lower(query), 'optimize|merge'), 'Merge / OPTIMIZE', match(lower(query), 'ttl'), 'TTL', 'Other') AS source, count() AS query_count, sum(ProfileEvents['S3ReadRequestsCount']) AS total_s3_gets, round(avg(ProfileEvents['S3ReadRequestsCount'])) AS avg_gets_per_query FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.query_log) WHERE event_time >= toDateTime(intDiv($__from, 1000)) AND event_time <= toDateTime(intDiv($__to, 1000)) AND type = 'QueryFinish' AND ProfileEvents['S3ReadRequestsCount'] > 0 GROUP BY source ORDER BY total_s3_gets DESC

panels.title: Failed Replicated Part Fetches/sec
panels.description: Failed attempts to fetch a replicated part. Sustained failures indicate a broken replica or network issue.

panels.title: Network RX Imbalance Ratio — across Pods
panels.description: Ratio of busiest pod RX to quietest pod RX (max/min across all selected pods). 1.0 = perfectly balanced. A sustained value >2–3 means one pod is receiving disproportionately more traffic — likely a load balancer misconfiguration or a coordinator hot-spot in distributed queries.

panels.title: Total Active Parts — per Pod
panels.description: Total active MergeTree parts. A rising trend means merges are not keeping pace with inserts.

targets.rawSql: SELECT database, table, count() AS active_parts, sum(rows) AS total_rows, formatReadableSize(sum(bytes_on_disk)) AS size_on_disk FROM system.parts WHERE active = 1 AND database != 'system' GROUP BY database, table ORDER BY active_parts DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Parts per Partition — Top 20
panels.description: Partitions with the most active parts. High per-partition counts indicate merge lag within that partition.

targets.rawSql: SELECT database, table, partition, count() AS parts, formatReadableSize(sum(bytes_on_disk)) AS size FROM system.parts WHERE active = 1 AND database != 'system' GROUP BY database, table, partition ORDER BY parts DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Largest Parts by Size — Top 20
panels.description: Individual parts sorted by disk size. Useful for identifying unexpectedly large parts that may slow merges.

targets.rawSql: SELECT database, table, name, partition, rows, formatReadableSize(bytes_on_disk) AS size_on_disk, formatReadableSize(data_uncompressed_bytes) AS size_uncompressed FROM system.parts WHERE active = 1 AND database != 'system' ORDER BY bytes_on_disk DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Detached Parts — per Node
panels.description: Detached parts are excluded from queries and merges. They accumulate due to replica repair, failed fetches, or manual detach. Non-zero counts require investigation.

targets.rawSql: SELECT hostname() AS node, database, table, reason, count() AS detached_parts FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.detached_parts) GROUP BY node, database, table, reason ORDER BY detached_parts DESC LIMIT 30

panels.title: Total Parts vs SELECT Latency — Correlation
panels.description: Overlay of total active part count (left axis) and average SELECT latency (right axis). A rising part count that tracks with rising latency confirms merge lag is degrading query performance.

panels.title: Mark Cache Hit Rate — per Pod
panels.description: Fraction of mark lookups served from cache. High part counts create more unique mark ranges, pushing out cached entries. A falling hit rate alongside a rising part count is a strong sign of merge lag affecting read performance.

panels.title: Too Many Parts — Current Error State
panels.description: Shows TOO_MANY_PARTS errors from system.errors across all nodes. When this fires, ClickHouse slows or blocks inserts into the affected table until merges catch up.

targets.rawSql: SELECT hostname() AS node, name AS error, value AS count, last_error_message AS message, toDateTime(last_error_time) AS last_seen FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.errors) WHERE name = 'TOO_MANY_PARTS' AND value > 0 ORDER BY count DESC

panels.title: Oldest Active Part per Table
panels.description: Age in hours of the oldest active part per table. A very old part in a heavily written table suggests merges have stalled on that table — check merge pool saturation and TOO_MANY_PARTS errors.

targets.rawSql: SELECT database, table, max(dateDiff('hour', modification_time, now())) AS oldest_part_hours, count() AS active_parts FROM system.parts WHERE active = 1 AND database != 'system' GROUP BY database, table ORDER BY oldest_part_hours DESC LIMIT 20
